newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm amid late commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm amid late commercial buying.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled firm and near their intraday highs amid late commercial buying, traders said.
Wheat had been buoyed throughout the session by harvest delays and by bullish export news.
"The reason we gained late was we saw commercial buying by (Cargill Investor Services)," a KCBT trader said. Another trader said Continental bought the September contract late.
KCBT wheat gained early after heavy rains fell overnight in Kansas, bringing a halt to harvesting activity Thursday and possibly into the weekend.
Additional support came from news Algeria bought U.S. hard red winter wheat and Tunisia tendered to buy 150,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
KCBT wheat settled 1/2 cent lower to 5-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up five cents at $3.45-1/4. September gained 5-1/4 cents to close at its intraday high of $3.54.

The early firmness in KCBT wheat triggered some technical short covering in the July and September contracts, traders said. Speculative players were also active buyers of the July/Sept spread in order to roll out short positions.

Featured players on the spread included ADM's Benson-Quinn Commodities, which bull-spread 3.5 million July/Sept at 6-1/2 to seven cents per bushel. Refco bull-spread one million July/Sept at 6-1/2 to 7-1/2 cents.

In flat price activity, Continental Grain, FIMAT Futures, Linnco, Prudential Securities and Rosenthal Collins each bought around one million Sept bushels. Prudential and FIMAT each sold at least 1.5 million Sept.
